claim: Canonicalize the already validated 32x32 temporal/is-was finite causal response matrix, after a frozen task-balanced diagonal scaling, and classify leading modes by source-task, target-task, family, and intervention-direction support.
novelty: The parent proves an eight-state weight-predicted realization but does not identify its canonical operational modes or distinguish task-shared from task-specific source and reader modes. This is a zero-forward analysis of the frozen causal matrix, not another activation-rank fit.
measurements: rank-k reconstruction error in every task quadrant
per-mode source and target task energy
per-mode cosine with the registered intervention-direction sign vector

predictions.shared_mode: At least one leading task-balanced mode has at least 10% source and target energy in each task.
predictions.direction_mode: At least one of the first four source or target mode vectors has absolute direction-sign cosine at least .70.
predictions.finite_predictability: The first eight exact and weight-predicted task-balanced subspaces agree at mean squared canonical cosine at least .90.
predictions.non_scalar: Rank one fails to reconstruct at least one quadrant to 10% relative RMSE while rank eight reconstructs every quadrant to 1%.

null: If leading modes segregate by task or weight-predicted and exact canonical subspaces disagree, the current shared-Q8 realization remains a predictive interface but does not identify a shared computational vocabulary.
